answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each agent stake reputation inside a verifiable kernel of past work: before an agent can join a shared market, it must publish a signed history of completed tasks that peers can audit. Creating a fake identity then costs real compute and real time, like building a reef coral by coral, so one attacker cannot cheaply spawn thousands of shells. Newcomers start on a low terrace with capped rewards and rise only as their attested history grows, so flooding the network with sock puppets buys no influence without paying the full cost of earning trust first.
